strengths: Exemplary ablation study (Table 1) systematically demonstrates the value of each component with clear empirical evidence for nonlinear compression over PCA and synergistic local-global-latent modeling
Strong empirical results: 60.9% FID improvement over SiT-B/2 baseline; reaches 1M-step REG performance (2.7 FID) with ~30% fewer iterations; consistent gains across model scales and generation modes
Semantic preservation validated beyond FID: attentive probing (Fig. 4) and semantic segmentation experiments (Fig. 6) demonstrate nonlinear compressor preserves VFM information better than PCA

Thorough design analysis: compression dimensionality (Fig. 5), model capacity (Table 5), VFM layer selection (Table 6), and cross-VFM robustness (Table 8) provide comprehensive justification for choices
Practical efficiency: negligible parameter increase (130M→132M), lightweight compressor (16.6M params), maintains inference efficiency with minimal throughput reduction
Clear presentation: well-written with informative figures/tables; reproducibility supported by detailed appendices and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: core contribution is primarily engineering—replacing PCA with standard CNN autoencoder and concatenating three modalities. Semantic compressor is basic (3-layer CNN); external alignment loss from prior work. Lacks fundamental innovation

Restricted experimental scope: single dataset (ImageNet) and resolution (256×256) only; no higher-resolution experiments despite mentioning them; limited to ImageNet for unconditional generation; scope acknowledged as resource-constrained but limits generalizability

Unfair baseline comparisons: Table 4 compares 160-epoch REGLUE against 800-epoch REPA/ReDi/REG (5× difference); paper acknowledges but claims competitiveness anyway; no error bars or confidence intervals on FID scores

Missing theoretical understanding: no explanation for why nonlinear compression fundamentally outperforms PCA; no information-theoretic analysis; optimal 16-channel choice lacks principled justification; mechanisms of improvement unexplained

Heavy VFM dependency with limited robustness: CLIP-L significantly underperforms (18.1 vs. 12.9 FID); no analysis of what makes certain VFMs suitable; method cannot work without strong pretrained VFMs; cross-VFM generalization unclear

Incomplete computational cost analysis: while parameters constant, actual training/inference overhead not fully quantified; Table 5 shows throughput degrades substantially (32,304→9,510 samples/sec) with larger compressors; cost implications for practitioners unclear

Hyperparameter complexity without full sensitivity analysis: multiple hyperparameters (compression channels, hidden size, VFM layers, λs, λcls, λrep); different alignment layers across model sizes; limited exploration of full sensitivity space

Scalability limitations: XL/2 experiments limited to 1M steps due to resources; ultra-long training behavior unknown; no exploration of truly large models; limits assessment of method's utility for future large-scale systems

Limited negative results and failure analysis: no discussion of scenarios where joint modeling hurts; when linear compression suffices; failure modes beyond resource constraints; conditions for applicability undefined

State-of-the-art gaps not deeply analyzed: autoregressive models (VAR, MAR) outperform on FID (Table 4); fundamental performance gaps versus LDMs not discussed; positioning relative to future paradigms unclear

strengths: Comprehensive ablation study (Table 1) with systematic decomposition of local semantics, global token, nonlinear compression, and external alignment contributions

Thorough semantic preservation analysis using attentive probing (Fig. 4) and semantic segmentation (Fig. 6) to validate that aggressive compression retains meaningful semantics

Extensive experimental validation across multiple model sizes, training schedules, evaluation metrics (FID, sFID, IS, Precision, Recall), different VFMs, data-limited regimes, and both conditional/unconditional generation
Comprehensive implementation details and reproducibility specifications enabling reproduction
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: the contribution is primarily an engineering combination of existing techniques (standard CNN autoencoder compressor, straightforward multimodal velocity prediction, REPA-style alignment); no fundamentally new algorithmic ideas
Incremental and scale-dependent improvements: 2.3 FID gain on SiT-B/2 (15% relative), but only 0.2 FID on SiT-XL/2 at 1M steps (7.4% relative); gains diminish significantly at larger scales

Insufficient mechanistic explanation of why nonlinear compression works: ablations show it does work but lack insight into the underlying reasons; architecture choices (layer selection, hidden dimensions) appear empirically driven without principled justification
Heavy dependency on VFM quality: 40% FID degradation with CLIP-L vs DINOv2-B (18.1 vs 12.9 FID); limited discussion of this critical dependency or applicability when high-quality VFMs are unavailable

Questionable framing of synergistic benefits: setting (i) with only nonlinear local compression achieves 14.3 FID; adding global token and alignment yields only 1.4 FID improvement, suggesting the semantic compressor alone drives most gains

Limited experimental scope: only 256×256 resolution; only ImageNet evaluation; SiT-XL/2 limited to 1M iterations due to compute constraints; higher resolutions and diverse datasets would strengthen claims

Unexplored design choices and hyperparameter sensitivity: no ablation on λ_s=1, λ_cls=0.03, λ_rep=0.5; missing empirical justification for channel-wise fusion vs alternatives; no sensitivity analysis for robustness
Insufficient discussion of failure modes, when spatial VFM guidance is unhelpful, and computational cost overhead during training from the compressor and alignment loss

strengths: Excellent ablation study (Table 1) systematically validating each component contribution, showing non-linear compression yields 7.1 FID improvement over ReDi's linear PCA
Strong and consistent empirical results across multiple scales and settings with significant convergence acceleration (25-30% fewer iterations to match baselines)

Comprehensive experimental analysis including multiple metrics, conditional/unconditional generation, semantic preservation validation via probing and segmentation tasks, and data efficiency evaluation
Technically sound approach with clear motivation: joint modeling of VAE latents, compressed spatial semantics, and global tokens is well-formulated and addresses limitations of prior work
Thorough semantic compressor analysis with detailed ablations on dimensionality, capacity, and layer selection, demonstrating that learned non-linear compression better preserves semantics than PCA
Good presentation with clear writing, informative visualizations (especially Figure 1 and Table 1), and promised code release supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (lightweight autoencoders, multimodal joint modeling from ReDi, external alignment from REPA) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts

Narrow experimental scope limiting generalizability claims: evaluation restricted to ImageNet 256×256 only, no text-to-image, COCO, or other domains; no higher resolutions (512×512); only SiT models tested

Incremental and diminishing gains in high-compute regimes: Table 4 shows only 0.06 FID improvement over REG at 160 epochs; at 800 epochs REPA (1.42) outperforms REGLUE (1.53), suggesting limited advantage at large scale
Frozen semantic compressor without end-to-end joint optimization: separate offline pretraining may be suboptimal; unclear if joint training would yield better results

Unexpected and unexplained phenomenon: Table 7 shows that adding standard regularization (KL, GAN losses) hurts compressor performance—needs deeper analysis

Limited analysis of learned representations: no visualizations of attention/features to explain why joint modeling works; probing validates preservation but doesn't reveal what spatial structure is learned
Fairness concerns in baseline comparisons: REPA/ReDi/REG from concurrent NeurIPS 2025 work with potentially different implementations/hyperparameters; official implementations would strengthen claims

Some presentation issues: informal title 'REGLUE Your Latents'; dense notation; key architectural details relegated to appendix

strengths: Excellent ablation study (Table 1) systematically decomposing contributions of local/global semantics, linear/non-linear compression, and external alignment; clearly shows patch-level spatial semantics outperform global-only signals

Efficient design maintaining inference-time throughput (3.8 img/s, same as REG) through channel-wise fusion, avoiding quadratic attention cost of concatenation while achieving significant FID improvements (60.9% over vanilla SiT-B/2)

Comprehensive semantic preservation analysis with probing accuracy (Figure 2), diffusability diagnostic showing high-frequency suppression (Figure 3), and semantic segmentation validation (68.7 mIoU with 16-channel compression vs 72.5 full features)

Thorough experimental validation across multiple metrics (FID, sFID, IS, Precision, Recall, CMMD, FD), both conditional/unconditional generation, model scales (B/XL), datasets (ImageNet, Food-101, ImageNet-512), and data-limited regimes with extensive ablations

Practical value of 30% training iteration reduction to match baseline performance; well-positioned for practitioners; promised code release and sufficient implementation details support reproducibility

Clear insights that non-linear compression significantly outperforms linear PCA with multiple layers (14.3 vs 21.4 FID over ReDi) and that patch-level spatial guidance is critical despite external alignment being complementary
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: joint VAE-latent + VFM-feature modeling already demonstrated by ReDi, multi-layer feature aggregation is straightforward concatenation, global [CLS] + alignment borrowed from REG; main contribution (non-linear compressor) is an engineering optimization rather than fundamental advance

Semantic compressor design lacks principled justification: no exploration of alternative architectures (transformer-based, knowledge distillation), unclear why 256 hidden dimensions is optimal beyond empirical ablation, connection between diffusability (Figure 3) and generation quality is empirical rather than analytical

Incomplete understanding of failure modes: setting (j) multi-layer PCA yields 23.1 FID versus 13.3 for non-linear multi-layer—a 9.8 FID gap warranting deeper investigation; setting (f) global-only alignment degrades performance, but mechanism ('unstable without spatial anchors') is superficial; why channel-wise addition outperforms alternatives lacks semantic justification

Limited evaluation scope: primarily ImageNet 256×256; XL experiments capped at 1M iterations (not ultra-long 4M training); no evaluation on other domains (COCO, artistic images) or generalization to non-SiT diffusion frameworks

Significant dependency on VFM quality underexplored: CLIP-L performs substantially worse (18.1 FID) than DINOv2-B (12.9); which VFM properties are essential (dimensionality, self-supervised pretraining) unclear, limiting transferability

Missing sensitivity analyses: no ablation on loss weights (λs=1, λcls=0.03, λrep=0.5), noise schedule interactions with semantic guidance unexplored, CFG ablations only for one configuration, compressor hidden dimensionality optimized empirically without principled explanation

Comparison framing concerns: main results mix different training epochs (REG/ReDi 800 epochs vs REGLUE 80 in Table 4); '30% fewer iterations' claim should specify regime (1M-step, SiT-XL/2 context); efficiency gains are real but narrative could be more precise

Technical clarity issues: dense notation in Section 3.2 could be simplified; semantic justification for channel-wise fusion (Eq. 5) is missing (justified only by efficiency); 'entanglement' framing oversells what is essentially feature fusion; critical details (compressor training) relegated to appendix

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear articulation of limitations in prior work (REG's global-only approach, ReDi's linear PCA)
Systematic ablation studies (Table 1) that methodically decompose component contributions
Comprehensive semantic preservation analysis combining probing accuracy, segmentation tasks, and diffusability diagnostics
Efficient design avoiding computational overhead through channel-wise fusion instead of sequence concatenation
Broad experimental coverage including multiple VFMs, scales, limited-data regimes, and diverse metrics beyond FID
Thorough implementation details and reproducibility considerations with promised code release
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core contribution is replacing ReDi's linear PCA with a CNN autoencoder—a straightforward engineering optimization rather than a novel method

Overstated claims about preserving 'nonlinear' semantics: the compressor is trained on reconstruction loss (Eq. 11), not explicitly optimized for semantic fidelity; unclear whether improvements stem from better compression or better semantic preservation
Modest practical improvements: 12.9 vs 15.2 FID over REG at 400K steps (~15%) and 1.46 vs 1.59 at equal epochs (~9% with CFG); minimal gain from external alignment (0.2 FID from REPA loss alone)

High sensitivity to design choices: layer selection (16.9 FID with early layers vs 13.3 with late layers), VFM choice (DINOv3-B outperforms DINOv2-B by 0.6 FID), and hyperparameters lack principled justification or sensitivity analysis

Unfair experimental comparisons: mixing different iteration counts across tables (e.g., 300K REGLUE vs 400K REG); limited baseline diversity (only compares to REPA/ReDi/REG; no ablation against alternative compression methods)

Limited scalability and generalization: experiments predominantly at 256×256 resolution; acknowledged 7-day training constraint for SiT-XL/2 at 1M steps; unclear if method generalizes to other diffusion backbones (only SiT tested)

Shallow theoretical understanding: no clear explanation for why channel-wise fusion is fundamentally better beyond computational efficiency, why specific layer combinations (9-12) work, or what each component contributes to final performance
Semantic preservation analysis relies on indirect evidence (probing accuracy, segmentation) without directly validating whether generation-relevant semantics are preserved better than with PCA

strengths: Comprehensive experimental analysis with systematic ablations (Table 1) clearly demonstrating the contribution of each component; shows local semantics >> global, nonlinear >> linear compression (7.1 FID gap vs ReDi)

Strong empirical results with consistent improvements (SiT-B/2: 33.0→12.9 FID, 47.1% reduction vs REPA; SiT-XL/2: 30% faster convergence) validated across multiple metrics (FID, sFID, IS, Precision, Recall, CMMD, FD∞)

Excellent semantic preservation analysis via multiple approaches: attentive probing (Figure 2), semantic segmentation (67.1 mIoU vs 59.1 PCA), and interpretable DCT frequency analysis (Figure 3) explaining why nonlinear compression aids diffusion

Practical efficiency with no computational overhead: identical parameters (132M) and throughput (3.8 img/s) to baselines; lightweight compressor trains in <1 hour; channel-wise fusion strategy cleverly avoids quadratic attention costs

Thorough experimental scope: validated across VFM choices (DINOv2, DINOv3, CLIP), limited-data regimes (5.5 FID gain at 20%), multiple datasets (Food-101, ImageNet-512), conditional/unconditional generation, and numerous ablations (compression dims, hidden sizes, layer selection, fusion strategy)
Clear problem identification: paper effectively argues that prior work under-utilizes rich VFM semantics by either discarding spatial structure (REG) or applying lossy linear compression (ReDi)
Well-presented and reproducible: code promised to be released, detailed hyperparameters provided, clear mathematical formulation, multiple validation approaches beyond generation metrics
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: the semantic compressor is a standard CNN autoencoder; core components (VFM alignment, spatial features, joint modeling) are individually known; primary contribution is engineering/combination rather than introducing fundamentally new mechanisms

Narrow evaluation scope: primarily ImageNet 256×256 experiments; no text-to-image, video, 3D, or other generative tasks; higher-resolution (512×512) only in supplementary; SiT-XL/2 limited to 1M steps by compute constraints, preventing full convergence study; only tested on SiT architecture

Critical VFM dependency: method performance highly sensitive to VFM quality (CLIP-L yields 18.1 vs 12.9 FID); no principled guidance for VFM or layer selection beyond empirical sweeps; introduces external dependency on frozen pretrained models with unclear long-term stability as VFMs evolve

Incomplete theoretical justification: why is 16-channel compression optimal? (Table 5 shows empirical sweet spot but lacks principled derivation); DCT frequency analysis shallow; layer selection (9-12 vs other combinations) appears somewhat arbitrary despite Table 7 optimization; missing ablation on loss weights (λs, λcls, λrep sensitivity)

Comparison fairness concerns: baseline numbers (REG, ReDi) appear from prior papers without explicit reproduction in identical settings; default uses DINOv2-B but DINOv3-B is better (0.6 FID gap) - choice justified as consistency rather than optimality; compute comparisons in supplementary but minimized in main text

Configuration sensitivity revealed by Table 1: performance varies substantially with component configuration; multiple hyperparameters (compression dims, hidden sizes, alignment weight) with limited transferability guidance; fusion strategy trade-off (4% FID vs 55% throughput) underexplored

Missing ablations and design justifications: no sensitivity analysis for loss weights; KL regularization explicitly shown harmful (Appendix A.2) yet included as option; why is global token retained in final config when patches achieve 13.3 FID alone?; alignment layer choice (k=4, k=8) lacks sensitivity study

Clarity and notation issues: Section 3.2 dense notation in Eqs. 3-6 difficult to parse; motivation for specific layer selection (9-12) introduced post-hoc in experiments; channel-wise vs sequence fusion justified primarily by efficiency rather than principled design; some choices (MSE loss for compressor) lack explicit justification

Incomplete reproducibility: code not available for review despite promises; training variance not shown (single runs or averaged?); hyperparameter robustness unclear (sensitivity to batch size, scheduling); random seed handling unspecified

Limited related work engagement: minimal discussion of other semantic-aware acceleration techniques beyond REPA/ReDi/REG; no comparison with non-VFM speedup methods (knowledge distillation, teacher-student); recent latent design work (FA-VAE) mentioned but not compared
